kh-0dYP.title: Landscape: wild, uncultivated northeast
kh-0dYP.summary: In the northeast, there is less farming and more natural vegetation, with some slightly hilly areas.

kh-1PXc.title: Chevron: black with yellow arrows
kh-1PXc.summary: Curve signs are black with yellow arrows. They are rare, since bollards often mark curves instead. All other Southeast Asian countries use yellow with black arrows, the reverse.

differs.how: Thailand's chevrons are yellow with black arrows

kh-2RXL.title: Sign: Chinese writing next to local script
kh-2RXL.summary: Signs with Chinese writing alongside the local language are common in Preah Sihanouk.

kh-2lvR.title: Landscape: red-soil jungle off-roads
kh-2lvR.summary: Unpaved jungle tracks in the southwest have red soil, dense jungle and hilly ground. Some eastern jungle roads look similar but with brown or orange soil.

kh-3k1I.title: Buildings: ornate Buddhist temples
kh-3k1I.summary: Most people are Buddhist, so decorated temples with ornamented roofs are common. Thailand and Laos have similar temples.

kh-4afK.title: Coverage: low-quality camera in the southwest
kh-4afK.summary: The low-quality camera is only found in the southwestern half of the country.

kh-5Ed2.title: Driving side: right
kh-5Ed2.summary: Traffic drives on the right. Thailand drives on the left, while Vietnam and Laos also drive on the right.

kh-6wbR.title: Road lines: yellow centre, rare white edge
kh-6wbR.summary: Dashed or solid yellow centre lines. Edge lines are rare and solid white when present. Thailand uses similar lines.

kh-7UIH.title: Pole: concrete ladder pole or round holed pole
kh-7UIH.summary: Two common types: concrete ladder poles with ridges, and round concrete poles with small holes. Rare wooden poles exist. Vietnam has the same round poles. Thailand uses square poles with rows of tiny holes, which are rare here.

differs.how: Thailand uses square concrete poles with rows of tiny pinholes

kh-Bp20.title: Soil: sandy white ground
kh-Bp20.summary: Sandy white soil, from bright white to beige, is very common southeast of the capital and around it. It appears elsewhere less often, and some roads here have darker soil.

kh-Djem.title: Road: wide unpaved brown road in open jungle
kh-Djem.summary: The northern part of Road 76 is a wide unpaved road with brown soil and semi-open jungle all around. Skies are overcast in the south and nearly clear in the north. Other roads can look similar but this is the longest.

kh-E31g.title: Houses: wooden stilt houses, vertical planks
kh-E31g.summary: Wooden houses raised on stilts are common. Walls are often vertical planks and many roofs are double or triple layered.

kh-EFcY.title: Bollard: red-and-white stone
kh-EFcY.summary: Most common are a stone bollard with red-and-white stripes, and a stone bollard with a red top and white base, usually with a reflector in the red part. Some designs belong to single roads.

kh-JTi1.title: Coverage: overcast, big mountains, dirt road
kh-JTi1.summary: Near Phnum Samkos: overcast skies, big mountains in the distance, unpaved brown roads and wild, very green vegetation.

kh-Knff.title: Ads: Angkor, Anchor and Cambodia beer
kh-Knff.summary: Lots of adverts for the beers Angkor, Anchor and Cambodia Beer.

kh-MWhC.title: Google car: striped car or ridged antenna
kh-MWhC.summary: Gen 3 has two cars: one with a short stubby antenna with three ridges, and a white car with no antenna, a white stripe on the left and a yellow stripe on the right. The striped car is unique here.

differs.how: Bangladesh also has a striped car, but with different stripes

kh-Nned.title: Coverage: low-quality brownish camera
kh-Nned.summary: A poor camera with a wide circular car blur and brownish colours. Good maps rarely include it. India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Nepal have the same camera.

kh-NpbG.title: Landscape: hills and low mountains
kh-NpbG.summary: The southwest is the highest part, with hills and low mountains. Inland roads can have dense forest, while the coast is quite densely populated.

kh-TMCo.title: Plants: rubber tree plantations in rows
kh-TMCo.summary: Rubber trees have thin trunks and dark green crowns in neat rows, often with small taps near the base. Found in a belt northeast of the capital, around Ban Lung and around Pech Sreada. Common in Thailand too, so use only to place yourself inside the country.

kh-VDZi.title: Road: only one side paved, red soil
kh-VDZi.summary: The road between Road 48 and Kiri Sakor is under construction, with just one paved side and red soil on the unpaved side.

kh-Vzui.title: Houses: orange or red tiled roofs
kh-Vzui.summary: Many traditional homes have orange or red tiled roofs, sometimes with ornaments on the ridges. Plain or corrugated metal roofs are also common. Newer buildings vary.

kh-XnE4.title: Houses: red-brown or blue walls, blue trim
kh-XnE4.summary: Traditional stilt houses have walls painted dark red-brown, light blue or ochre orange, with bright blue doors and windows. Newer houses use more colours.

kh-bFGl.title: Coverage: limited, around big cities
kh-bFGl.summary: Street View is patchy. Most of it is around the capital, Siem Reap and Battambang.

kh-cjig.title: Landscape: mountain ridge to the north, red soil
kh-cjig.summary: Near the northern Thai border, a mountain ridge runs along the horizon to your north, with red soil. The road itself is on a very flat lowland below the ridge.

differs.how: Thai side is higher, but looks similar from the border

kh-gL9F.title: Pole: three beams, insulators on one side
kh-gL9F.summary: Along Road 6 west of Siem Reap to Sisophon, and Road 5 south of Sisophon to Battambang, poles have three horizontal beams with hanging insulators on one side only, and indents at the bottom. Found nowhere else here.

kh-hIEP.title: Roads: many are unpaved
kh-hIEP.summary: Many roads are unpaved. Usually only main roads and roads in or near towns are paved.

kh-hIz3.title: Pole: three beams, insulators on both sides
kh-hIz3.summary: The same powerline continues on Road 5 west of Sisophon, but the insulators hang on both sides. The rest of the pole is the same.

kh-iFSu.title: Plants: oil palm plantations
kh-iFSu.summary: Oil palms only grow on Road 4 and some side roads just north of Preah Nob. They are far more common in Malaysia and Indonesia, so use this only once you know it's Cambodia.

kh-ie5M.title: Coverage: overcast, dark tarmac, edge lines
kh-ie5M.summary: The southern part of Road 76 has overcast weather, dark asphalt, outer road lines and crisp markings by local standards. Much of the east side runs through hilly dense jungle.

kh-j4t2.title: Bollard: black-and-white, one road only
kh-j4t2.summary: Black-and-white bollards appear in Cambodia only on Road 48 between Tatai and Road 4. Thailand uses them commonly, so check other clues first.

kh-llUG.title: Sign: blue political party signs
kh-llUG.summary: Blue signs from the ruling party across the country, often with three men's faces side by side.

kh-lm-12981.title: Sign: stop sign with Khmer and English
kh-lm-12981.summary: Stop signs always have the Khmer word (ឈប់) as well as the English word STOP.

kh-mBby.title: Road: wide red-brown shoulders
kh-mBby.summary: Road 4 between Angk Snuol and Preah Sihanouk mostly has wide red-brown shoulders on both sides. Near the capital they are paler, pinkish or beige; in the hills and near the coast they are darker.

kh-mIwy.title: Landscape: white rocky plateau, stunted bushes
kh-mIwy.summary: Preah Monivong National Park is a highland plateau with white, very rocky soil and low windswept bushes in a dark green tint. Some parts are more forested but keep the rocky soil.

kh-mdL7.title: Route marker: stone, white base, red top
kh-mdL7.summary: Stone road markers with a white base and a rounded red top. The road number is on the narrow side and a town name with distance on the wide side.

kh-mhzQ.title: Landscape: flat farmland with villages
kh-mhzQ.summary: The low central plain holds most of the farmland: flat, cultivated land dotted with villages and farms.

kh-sIUL.title: Language: Khmer script, curvy and intricate
kh-sIUL.summary: Khmer has its own script with intricate, curvy letters, though fonts vary a lot. Thai and Lao look similar but are less intricate, and simple Khmer fonts can resemble them.

kh-vddA.title: Plants: dry-season rubber trees, orange soil
kh-vddA.summary: Around Pech Sreada in the far east, rubber plantations were filmed in the dry season, giving them a distinct look, and the soil is very orange.

kh-wmTo.title: Plate: white with blue letters
kh-wmTo.summary: White plates with blue letters. The blue sheen is hard to see through the blur, so they can look plain white. Government vehicles have green plates.

kh-xNF2.title: Bollard: triangular with red stripes
kh-xNF2.summary: Triangular bollards with red stripes appear only in the southwest: on Road 4 (mainly Kirirom to Preah Sihanouk), one off-road in Ream National Park, and Preah Monivong National Park.

kh-xU6h.title: Road: wide grey gravel, runs north-northeast
kh-xU6h.summary: Road 41 is wide with a grey, gravelly surface and runs roughly north-northeast. The land beside it is flat farmland, with hills often seen in the distance. Road angle is key since other roads look similar.

kh-zw5H.title: Landmark: dark weathered stone temple complex
kh-zw5H.summary: Angkor Wat, just north of Siem Reap, has a huge complex of dark, weathered stone buildings. It has lots of walking-camera coverage and is common on GeoGuessr's official map, but rare in competitive maps.
